title: Parallax Predicate Algebra (m-predicate)
description: Canonical, format-agnostic serialization of an m-predicate Predicate node: the RECURSIVE Boolean selection grammar and nothing else. Each node is a single-key tagged object. Every query-wide value — the queried position, result narrowing, ordering, the row cap, Temporal Selection, and Includes — is a sibling clause of the Object Query that carries this predicate (object-query.schema.json), so recursion buys composition of selection logic alone. The narrow node here is PREDICATE-SCOPED: it restricts the active position while evaluating its inner predicate, which is a filter rather than whole-result narrowing. Physical interval predicates are injected by m-temporal-read and never authored in a Predicate. The nodes cover the full scalar, string, membership, range, null, Boolean, relationship, nested-value-object, and inheritance-narrowing algebra.

attributeRef.description: A metamodel attribute reference of the form Entity.attribute, whose Entity segment is bare or namespace-qualified (identity.schema.json).

relationshipRef.description: A metamodel relationship reference of the form Entity.relationship, whose Entity segment is bare or namespace-qualified (identity.schema.json).

literal.description: A scalar literal value usable as a bind.

stringMatch.description: A string predicate. `value` is a plain string; `like`/`notLike` interpret `%`/`_` as wildcards, the affix forms (startsWith/endsWith/contains) treat `value` as a literal and the implementation escapes wildcards. `caseInsensitive` defaults to false.

group.description: An explicit precedence-nesting node. It wraps a single inner operation so that a fluent or prefix surface that intends to group a sub-expression serializes to one unambiguous canonical form.

navigationFilter.description: Filter the queried entity by traversing a relationship. `rel` names the relationship; the optional `op` constrains the related entity. With no `op` it is a pure existence check.

navigate.description: navigate(rel) -> predicate: filter via traversal to a related entity. Lowers to a correlated EXISTS semi-join, so a to-many navigation never multiplies parent rows.

exists.description: exists(rel[, op]): the queried entity has at least one related row (optionally matching `op`). Lowers to a correlated EXISTS.

notExists.description: notExists(rel[, op]): the queried entity has no related row (optionally matching `op`). Lowers to a correlated NOT EXISTS.

narrow.description: narrow(to, operand): constrain the POLYMORPHIC position supplied by context to a Subtype Selection (m-predicate, m-inheritance). This is PREDICATE-SCOPED narrowing and therefore a filter: the position comes from where the node sits — the enclosing expression's active position for a Boolean term, the relationship target inside a navigation filter, and the enclosing selection's resolved set for a narrow nested in another narrow's operand. Whole-result narrowing is `narrowTo` on the Object Query and has no spelling here. `operand` is evaluated over the narrowed position. Model-aware validation resolves the selection, requires a non-empty subset of the active position, and threads that resolved set into `operand`; SQL lowering lifts the narrow into tag/branch selection (m-sql).

nestedRef.description: A reference into a valueObject's inner field: an Entity spelling (bare or namespace-qualified, identity.schema.json) and its valueObject followed by one or more dotted path segments into the embedded document (e.g. Customer.address.city, Customer.address.geo.lat). Lowers to a dialect-specific text extraction on the value object's backing column (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedComparison.description: A nested-field comparison: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) compared against a TYPED literal. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (first segment a declared valueObject on the entity, intermediates nested valueObjects, leaf a declared attribute); the `value` is a polymorphic `literal` whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type (m-predicate). The dialect-specific document extraction (m-sql/m-dialect) casts to that declared type before comparing.

nestedRange.description: A nested-field range test: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) bounded below and above by TYPED literals. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`); BOTH bounds are `literal`s whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type (m-predicate). A `lower` strictly greater than its `upper` names an empty range and MUST be rejected (m-predicate bound-ordering rule), checked AFTER the typed-literal rule so a mistyped bound is named as such. Lowers to one `<extraction> between ? and ?` — never two comparisons — with the JSON path bind(s) first, then `lower`, then `upper` (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedMembership.description: A nested-field membership test: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) tested against a non-empty list of TYPED literals. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`); each list value is a `literal` whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type (m-predicate). Lowers to `<extraction> in (?, ?, …)` — negated with a leading `not` for `nestedNotIn` — with the JSON path bind(s) first, then one bind per list value in order (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedStringMatch.description: A nested-field string predicate: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) matched against a pattern or a literal affix. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`) and its leaf's declared type MUST be `String`; a string predicate aimed at any other member is `nested-string-predicate-non-string-member`, checked BEFORE the typed-literal rule so a `date` / `time` / `timestamp` / `uuid` / `bytes` member — which rides the portable string literal and so would otherwise pass the typed-literal check — is named rather than silently accepted (m-predicate). `value` carries the top-level `stringMatch` semantics unchanged: `%` and `_` are wildcards for `nestedLike` / `nestedNotLike`, while the affix forms (`nestedStartsWith` / `nestedEndsWith` / `nestedContains`) treat it as literal text whose wildcards the implementation escapes. `caseInsensitive` defaults to false and otherwise folds BOTH sides with `lower(...)`. Lowers to `<extraction> like ?` — `<extraction> not like ?` for `nestedNotLike`, the same infix negation the scalar `notLike` renders — with the JSON path bind(s) first, then the pattern, then the escape character when escaping actually changed the literal (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedNullCheck.description: A nested-field presence test: a valueObject inner attribute referenced by a dotted path, with NO compared value. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`). Per the absence-collapse rule (m-predicate) every 'not present' state — SQL NULL column, missing key, JSON `null`, non-object intermediate segment — yields SQL NULL from the extraction, so `nestedIsNull` matches exactly those rows and `nestedIsNotNull` its complement.

nestedEq.description: nestedEq(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute equals a typed literal.

nestedNotEq.description: nestedNotEq(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute differs from a typed literal.

nestedGt.description: nestedGt(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is greater than a typed literal (the extraction is cast to the declared type before comparing).

nestedGte.description: nestedGte(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is greater than or equal to a typed literal.

nestedLt.description: nestedLt(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is less than a typed literal.

nestedLte.description: nestedLte(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is less than or equal to a typed literal.

nestedBetween.description: nestedBetween(path, lower, upper): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute lies within an inclusive range of two typed literals. One canonical node, never two comparisons — through a `many` segment a SINGLE element must satisfy the whole range.

nestedIn.description: nestedIn(path, values): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is one of a non-empty list of typed literals.

nestedNotIn.description: nestedNotIn(path, values): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is NOT one of a non-empty list of typed literals. Through a `many` segment this keeps the uniform any-element reading — SOME element's member is not in the list — exactly as nestedNotEq does; the no-element reading is spelled nestedNotExists(path, where: nestedIn(…)).

nestedLike.description: nestedLike(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute matches a SQL pattern — `%` and `_` are wildcards and the pattern passes through unescaped.

nestedNotLike.description: nestedNotLike(path, value, caseInsensitive?): the negation of nestedLike, lowered as the infix `not like`. Through a `many` segment it keeps the uniform any-element reading — SOME element's member does not match the pattern.

nestedStartsWith.description: nestedStartsWith(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute begins with the LITERAL text `value`, whose own wildcards are escaped before the trailing `%` is appended.

nestedEndsWith.description: nestedEndsWith(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute ends with the LITERAL text `value` (escaped, then prefixed with `%`).

nestedContains.description: nestedContains(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute contains the LITERAL text `value` (escaped, then wrapped in `%`).

nestedIsNull.description: nestedIsNull(path): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is 'not present' (SQL NULL column, missing key, JSON null, or non-object intermediate — all collapsed per m-predicate).

nestedIsNotNull.description: nestedIsNotNull(path): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is present (the complement of nestedIsNull).

valueObjectRef.description: A path that TERMINATES at a valueObject member (not an inner attribute): an Entity spelling (bare or namespace-qualified, identity.schema.json) and its valueObject, optionally followed by nested valueObject segments (e.g. Customer.address, Customer.address.phones). Unlike `nestedRef` — which requires an ATTRIBUTE leaf and so carries at least two member segments — this path may carry just one, because its subject is the value OBJECT itself. It resolves against the declared structure (first member segment a declared valueObject on the entity, each further segment a nested valueObject declared on the preceding member); the final member's multiplicity (`one` / `many`) selects the presence vs non-empty semantics of nestedExists/nestedNotExists (m-predicate).

elementRef.description: An ELEMENT-RELATIVE path used ONLY inside a scoped `where` (nestedExists/nestedNotExists over a `many` member). It carries NO Entity spelling — the subject is the array element bound by the enclosing exists — so it is one or more lowercase-initial dotted segments naming declared members of that element (`type`, `number`, or `geo.country` to descend a nested value object of the element). Each segment resolves against the element's declared structure (intermediates nested valueObjects, leaf a declared attribute).

elementComparison.description: An element-scoped nested comparison: an element-relative `path` compared against a TYPED literal whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type. The subject is the array element bound by the enclosing nestedExists/nestedNotExists `where`.

elementRange.description: An element-scoped nested range test: an element-relative `path` bounded below and above by TYPED literals whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type. One element must satisfy the WHOLE range, and the bound-ordering rule applies exactly as it does path-scoped.

elementMembership.description: An element-scoped membership test: an element-relative `path` tested against a non-empty list of typed literals.

elementStringMatch.description: An element-scoped string predicate: an element-relative `path` whose leaf's declared type MUST be `String`, matched against a pattern (`nestedLike` / `nestedNotLike`) or a literal affix (the three affix forms), with the same wildcard, escaping, and `caseInsensitive` semantics the path-scoped form carries.

elementNullCheck.description: An element-scoped presence test: an element-relative `path` with NO compared value.

elementPredicate.description: A scoped sub-predicate evaluated against ONE array element inside a nestedExists/nestedNotExists `where`. It is the flat `nested*` family re-expressed over element-relative paths (`elementRef`), composed with the ordinary boolean combinators. The whole compound must be satisfied by a SINGLE element (same-element semantics), which is what distinguishes it from ANDing flat any-element predicates at the top level (m-predicate).

nestedExistsBody.description: The body of nestedExists/nestedNotExists: a value-object-terminated `path` and an OPTIONAL element-scoped `where`. Without `where` the meaning is presence — a `one` member present (non-absent per the absence-collapse rule), a `many` member a NON-EMPTY array. With `where` (a `many` path), ONE element must satisfy the whole compound `where` sub-predicate (same-element semantics); nestedNotExists + where means NO element satisfies it (m-predicate). Lowers to the m-dialect array-traversal form (m-sql).

nestedExists.description: nestedExists(path[, where]): the value object at `path` is present (`one`) or its array is non-empty (`many`); with `where`, at least one element satisfies the compound sub-predicate.

nestedNotExists.description: nestedNotExists(path[, where]): the complement of nestedExists — the value object is absent (`one`) or the array is empty/absent (`many`); with `where`, no element satisfies the compound sub-predicate.
